data.narrative:
Perennial Autonomy operates in the Defense & Security sector at the government-contract stage, backed by Schmidt and a team with prior experience at SpaceX, Google, and Apple. The company has raised Schmidt-backed funding plus a $500M IDIQ contract. The relevant comp universe spans 23 same-sector peers, including 2 public companies (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private firms. Key private comparables include Anduril Industries, Helsing, Shield AI, Saronic, and Quantum-Systems.

Traditional peer-median valuation proved inapplicable due to insufficient narrow-stage peers. The Defense & Security sector lacks three or more comparable companies at Perennial Autonomy's specific stage and valuation tier, making same-stage or adjacent-stage multiples unreliable. A broader sector median would obscure meaningful differences in contract structure, technology maturity, and customer concentration across the 23 available peers.

Without a triangulated valuation from comparable multiples, this analysis cannot support a specific range. Determining fair value would require either: (i) deeper operational data from the two public comps to establish relevant multiples, (ii) transaction multiples from recent exits of private Defense & Security firms, or (iii) DCF modeling grounded in contract revenue visibility and margin assumptions. The $500M IDIQ provides revenue floor evidence but does not independently establish enterprise value. Key uncertainties include contract win probability, customer concentration risk, and technology defensibility relative to the named private peer set.
